node.description: Guy Korolevski and Yair Benamou, JFrog Security Researchers
node.title: Beyond testmetest: Native Addon Camouflage and 42 Armed GitHub Repositories Reveal a Hidden npm Publisher
node.excerpt: JFrog Security Research linked 42 armed GitHub repositories in the testmetest campaign to a hidden npm publisher, an active encrypted data sink and previously reported GitHub Actions cPanel exploitation infrastructure.

node.description: Aviv Engelberg, Eddy Tsalolikhin and Ofri Ouzan, JFrog Security Research
node.title: Brotli2Shell: Beyond Node(2Shell) and HTTP(2Shell)
node.excerpt: CVE-2026-111497 ("Brotli2Shell") is an out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder that reaches far beyond Node.js and HTTP. JFrog Security Research reproduced a remote crash in ClickHouse, native memory corruption in FFmpeg through JPEG XL, a .NET runtime crash, and an infinite loop in Apache Arrow, and released an open-source scanner that finds Brotli decoding paths version-only scanners miss.

node.description: Eddy Tsalolikhin and Afek Berger, JFrog Security Researcher
node.title: PHP2Shell: All You Need to Know About CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
node.excerpt: JFrog Security Research is tracking CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two CRITICAL-severity PHP core vulnerabilities (PHP2Shell) that turn unauthenticated requests into remote code execution and Heartbleed-style memory disclosure. We break down the bug flow, the shipped fix, and the fake PoCs that surfaced around the disclosure.

node.title: LiteLLM Hijacked Again: Malicious 1.107.0 Wheels Steal Credentials and Load Remote Code
node.excerpt: LiteLLM has been hijacked again: malicious `litellm` 1.107.0 wheels contain an interpreter-startup credential stealer and an hourly remote-code loader absent from the source distribution.

node.title: CVE-2026-92392: curl HTTP/2 upload RCE
node.excerpt: JFrog Security Research is tracking CVE-2026-92392, a HIGH-severity curl/libcurl use-after-free in HTTP/2 uploads that a malicious HTTPS server can turn into client-side remote code execution. We break down the bug, the published exploit, and the narrow conditions it needs.

node.title: Equation of Compromise: Anatomy of a Live npm Supply-Chain Campaign
node.excerpt: JFrog Security Research uncovered a targeted npm campaign hidden in cloned math libraries. The backdoor activates only for a specific matrix, receives encrypted tasks through an Ethereum Sepolia smart contract and Slack, and uses a GitHub Actions worker farm to manufacture hundreds of thousands of downloads.

node.title: New packages identified in GemStuffer 'OpenAI Swarm' malicious RubyGems campaign
node.excerpt: The JFrog Security Research team investigated the GemStuffer campaign done by rogue OpenAI agents - we found more than 3000 RubyGems packages associated with the coordinated attacks.

node.description: Aviv Engelberg and Niv Lanyado, JFrog Security Researchers
node.title: When "Critical" Loses Context: The Reality of Spring CVEs
node.excerpt: On August 20, 2026, Spring published 91 CVEs in a single day. CISA's ADP rated six of them Critical. When we checked those scores against Spring's own advisories, they didn't hold up.

node.title: Shai-Hulud Trinitite Hits @7nohe/openapi-react-query-codegen
node.excerpt: JFrog Security Research analyzed a new Mini Shai-Hulud wave on @7nohe/openapi-react-query-codegen. Ten npm versions drop a Trinitite-labeled worm through preinstall and an obfuscated binding.gyp command.

node.title: Compromised Rust crates on crates.io silently execute malware at build time
node.excerpt: On August 20th, the popular Rust crates arrayref, internment, and append-only-vec were compromised on crates.io. The malicious versions silently pulled in proc-macro1, a typosquat of proc-macro2, whose build.rs downloads and executes a remote payload on cargo build.
